canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: Both independent reviewers (epic-reviewer-1/claude-fable-5, epic-reviewer-2/gpt-5.5) returned pass with zero blocking findings, and their evidence is mutually consistent. The canonical pass independently re-verified every non-blocking finding against the current tree: package.json lines 27/29 confirm verify and verify-all are textually identical; src/inference/prompts/index.ts defines PROMPT_REGISTRY and DEFAULT_PROMPT_NAMES while src/index.ts re-exports only sdk.js and sdk.ts imports the registry solely for validation (line 343), confirming no exported name catalog; src/domains/turns/internal/derive.ts:85-88 confirms the sequential composeTurnRendering→projectLowerBand calls in one work item; test/inference-real.test.ts:120,178 confirms describe.runIf gating alongside the single accounting line built in test/fixtures/openrouter-call.ts:54-55; epic.md:3 still reads 'Status: Draft — pending review'; and team-impl-log.md retains 'Final Gate Status: not-run' (line 142) and the obsolete 'Story 5 BLOCKED awaiting LHC_OPENROUTER_KEY' open-risk note (line 146) despite the keyed-run receipt at line 109. The epic gate was re-run independently: exit 0, 40 test files, 377 passed, 9 env-gated keyed skips, exactly one visible 'NOT-RAN: real-inference (LHC_OPENROUTER_KEY unset)' line — matching both reviewers' gate reports. Reviewer-1's E05-NB-5 (epic.md Draft header) and reviewer-2's E05-NB-001 (stale team-impl-log closeout text) share a root cause and fix scope and are merged into one canonical finding. The only wording-level divergence between reviewers — the test plan's 'suite-level guard, not per-test skips' versus the implemented describe.runIf skips — is retained as a cosmetic observation since the run/not-run state remains one fact reported once. Ruling-020, flagged in the team-impl-log for epic-review ratification, is hereby ratified: the conditional landing-window exception (protected trailing turnless groups after the newest closed turn may lawfully leave the zone above target) is consistent with TC-5.2's already-sanctioned oversized-newest exception, is documented in the tech design's Flow 5 conditional-landing paragraph, and is enforced by implementation and tests; the absolute landing-window sentence in epic.md AC-5.3 should pick up the same qualifier at acceptance (folded into the stale-docs quick-fix finding).
crossStoryFindings: Story 2 → Story 3 seam handoff is coherent: createSdk's resolveInferenceProvider (src/sdk.ts:313) validates XOR, all seven FORM_KINDS by iterating the exported union, unknown kind keys, non-empty provider/model strings, and PROMPT_REGISTRY membership (src/sdk.ts:343), then drops the adapter into the same resolved.provider slot direct injection uses — everything downstream is unchanged Epic 02 code.

Story 3 → Story 4 reason-format coupling is consistent and ruling-backed: the adapter formats retryable reasons 'provider_failure: <kind>: <message>' and terminal reasons kind-led; the team-impl-log records the approved spec-deviation ruling, Story 4's classification tests consume the same format, and the queue's failAttempt/failTerminal copy the reason verbatim at exhaustion so forms land with the provider_failure-led reason AC-3.2 requires.

Story 4's machinery-untouched claim holds: FAILURE_CLASSIFICATION and safeCall live entirely in src/inference/classify.ts; the work-queue retains its Epic 02 shape with no inference-aware branches, satisfying the Chunk-4 exit gate (Epic 02 derivation suites green untouched).

Story 5 reuses Story 2's seam-conformance helpers parameterized over both hosts per DD-13: assertModelCallContract and assertRoutingThroughSdk run unchanged against the OpenRouter host, and the keyed receipt exists (2026-06-12, openai/gpt-5.4-mini, 13/13 pass, 'RAN: real-inference' accounting line, run twice).

Story 6 (boundary) and Story 1 (retirement) are cleanly independent of the inference pipeline as designed; the pipeline gate keeps the Epic 03 registration site, advance-before-poke order, and throw isolation untouched while gating on a turn_end-committed flag.

Provenance flows one direction across stories: stamped from config-known strings in the adapter, copied — never authored — by the messages handler and all three turns-side form writes (src/domains/turns/internal/derive.ts:101-104, 122-124); the deterministic provider sets none.
architectureFindings: Module architecture matches the tech design exactly: src/inference/{types,classify,adapter,prompts/*} exist as specified; the seven prompt modules are name-keyed in PROMPT_REGISTRY with versioned names; smoothing-v1 is the settled POC port and the other six carry pre-dial-in markers per AC-2.3.

The inference/ ↛ domains/ boundary rule is enforced in scripts/check-boundaries.mjs (independently confirmed: inference/ is grouped with tech-utils/shared in the may-not-import-domains check); inference/ imports only shared/ types, keeping the runtime graph one-directional.

DD-6/DD-7 resolved as designed: safeCall owns the per-call timeout (Promise.race, default 60_000) classifying as retryable timeout; summarizeToolResult input bounding is head-and-tail with marker under maxInputChars (default 200_000), applied before prompt rendering.

Flow 5 matches the design's conditional landing-window contract: advanceDecision is a pure function with whole-turn grouping (NULL turn_id degrading to singleton groups per DD-10), peek-ahead stop, open-turn exclusion from candidacy, and newest-closed-turn protection that structurally protects trailing turnless singletons; the shared-WHERE-clause invariant between status sum and decision walk holds, and the forward-only guard is in the UPDATE itself. Ruling-020 governing the landing-window exception is ratified by this review.

AC-5.4 lands fully: VisibilityBudgets is two-field with 64000/32000 defaults, maxTokens > targetTokens validated with a naming TypeError, and the retired floorTokens is rejected as unknown config citing the Epic 05 retirement.

Provider arrival is injection-only at createSdk: no bin in the package manifest, src/providers/registry.ts and src/cli are absent, and no LHC_PROVIDER, --provider, OpenRouter, or fetch path exists in production code; construction errors are TypeErrors naming the violated rule per the §Error Contract.
epicCoverageAssessment: All 22 ACs and 15 TCs across 6 flows trace to implementation and tests with a primary story owner in stories/coverage.md: the construction matrix parameterizes over FORM_KINDS, adversarial wrong-outcome canned text proves mechanical stamping, goldens exist for all seven templates, classification is asserted as data, golden G2 (30k/25k/20k/15k under 64k/32k landing at 35k) is implemented verbatim with the exact-target and oversized-newest legs, and retirement.test.ts proves the export snapshot, no bin, and zero LHC_PROVIDER/--provider references with the retired env var actively set.

Epic gate independently re-run by this canonical pass: verify-all exits 0 with 40 test files, 377 passed, 9 skipped — the 9 skips are exactly the env-gated keyed legs, with the single visible 'NOT-RAN: real-inference (LHC_OPENROUTER_KEY unset)' accounting line per AC-4.1.

The test plan's epic-acceptance condition for the capstone is satisfied: the team-impl-log records the DoD keyed-run receipt (2026-06-12, openai/gpt-5.4-mini, 13/13 pass, exactly one 'RAN: real-inference' line, run twice, verbose log retained), so the AC-4.2 integration-readiness gate has been exercised against a real endpoint.

The Epic 03 amendment ledger was applied (floor legs superseded by newest-turn protection, per-intake legs inverted to mid-turn-never-moves, G1 re-cut for turn grouping, floorTokens-rejection test added) and the red-manifest regenerated per the Story 6 commit; the Epic 04 parity-gap deviation note required by Flow 6 is recorded in the team-impl-log.
productionPathFindings: No fake adapters, shims, or placeholders in the production path: src/ contains no TODO/FIXME/not-implemented markers, no process.env reads, and no fetch calls — all network code lives in the test-owned OpenRouter fixture as the NFR requires.

All scripted/recording/throwing/hanging ModelCall fakes live in test/fixtures/model-call.ts, the spec-designated mock boundary for Flows 1–3 — boundary mocks, not internal mocks, per the testing strategy.

The deterministic marker-string provider survives only as the explicitly-injected CI test provider (DD-12); it cannot arrive silently — provider arrival is strict XOR injection at createSdk with no defaults, no registry, and no env fallback, verified by retirement.test.ts with LHC_PROVIDER actively set.

The OpenRouter ModelCall host is test-owned by design (DD-13, AC-4.1) — the proof-of-seam second host, not a production shim; the production host (PI extension) is explicitly out of scope for this epic.

The adapter's empty-output rule is enforced in the production path (whitespace-trimmed text rejected as retryable empty_output before any form lands ready), provenance is mechanically copied from config strings and never parsed from model output, and compact/pull/status/inspect/thread-view boundary code never invoke the model-call function.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Turn-derivation work item re-runs the rendering call when only the projection fails
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Independently confirmed at src/domains/turns/internal/derive.ts:85-88: composeTurnRendering and projectLowerBand are two sequential provider calls in one work item, so a retryable projection failure retries the whole item and re-invokes the rendering call. Worth weighing during dial-in if projection failures prove common.
